salesCopy.problem: You know you need a knowledge management system. You've probably tried building one before. But without a clear roadmap, most people make the same costly mistakes: picking tools before understanding their needs, building systems too complex to maintain, and forgetting critical components that make everything fall apart later.
problemPoints: Jumping into tools without knowing what you actually need
Building overly complex systems that require constant maintenance
Forgetting critical components like backups, habits, and maintenance routines
Taking notes you can never find when you need them
Starting and abandoning systems over and over again
No clear process to follow - just random note-taking
salesCopy.agitate: The frustration compounds. You set up a new system, feel excited for a week, then slowly stop using it. Your notes become another graveyard of good intentions. Worse: you might lose everything because you never thought about backups. Or your system grows stale because you forgot to build the habits that keep it alive. Without a complete picture of what a working system needs, you're building on sand.
agitatePoints: Systems that feel great at first but get abandoned within weeks
The sinking realization that you forgot something critical - like backups
Notes scattered everywhere because you skipped the planning phase
No consistent habits to keep your system alive and useful
Starting from scratch again and again, never making real progress
That nagging feeling: 'What am I missing?'

From foundation and planning (the phase most people skip) to continuous improvement (the phase most people forget). Use it to build your first system right, or audit your existing one to find the gaps.

originStory.title: Why This Checklist Exists
originStory.subtitle: From years of building and coaching
originStory.story:
After years of building my own systems and coaching professionals on knowledge management, I kept seeing the same patterns. People would jump into tools without planning. They'd forget about backups until disaster struck. They'd set up elaborate systems but never build the habits to maintain them.

This checklist is everything I wish I had when I started. And everything my coaching clients wish they'd had before making costly mistakes. It's the complete picture, distilled into actionable steps.

methodology.title: The 8-Phase Approach
methodology.subtitle: A complete roadmap, not just a feature list

steps.title: Phase 1: Foundation and Planning
steps.description: The phase most people skip. And the reason most systems fail. Define your goals, understand your needs, then choose your tools.

steps.title: Phases 2-5: Build and Connect
steps.description: System architecture, capture workflows, processing routines, and connection strategies that turn scattered notes into connected knowledge.

steps.title: Phase 6: Habits and Maintenance
steps.description: The most overlooked phase. Systems without habits become graveyards. Build the routines that keep your system alive.

steps.title: Phases 7-8: Optimize and Evolve
steps.description: Advanced optimization including AI integration, and continuous improvement strategies for long-term success.

methodology.philosophy: A knowledge system isn't a one-time setup. It's a living system that needs planning, habits, and continuous evolution. This checklist covers all of it.
methodology.differentiation: Most resources focus on tools and features. This checklist focuses on the complete system lifecycle - including the phases people forget about until it's too late.
